name: Exercise Demo
description: The workhorse: a cast member performs an exercise loop (push-ups, pull-ups, squats, planche, sprint, dead hang…) in manga ink with effort shake and sweat. The muscle / tendon / bone under discussion lights up red and pulses on the key word while a handwritten label with a curved red arrow points at it. Optional thumbnail title, rep counter and sets badge.

character.description: Who performs: rook (lean hero, default) or brick (hulking rival). Keep the same roles all video.

muscle.description: Body part highlighted in red (default: the exercise's main muscle).

label.description: Handwritten annotation pointing at the highlighted part (1–5 words, e.g. "Not muscle. Tendon.").

note.description: Optional second handwritten aside (1–4 words, e.g. "(at home)").

keyword.description: Narration word on which the red pulse, punch-in and label land (must appear in the narration).

title.description: Optional thumbnail-style bold title (2–6 words). Wrap one word in *asterisks* to make it red.

kicker.description: Optional tiny red tag above the title (1–3 words).

reps.description: Show the rep counter (default true for rep exercises).

period.description: Seconds per rep (1–4; default per exercise).

bg.description: Paper white (default) or ink black background. Pick one for a whole chapter.

exampleNarration: Every pull-up loads something most people never train on purpose: your tendons. They sit between muscle and bone, and they adapt slowly, but once they do, you can hold forces that pure muscle never could.

name: Anatomy Zoom
description: X-ray cut-away of an arm, leg or forearm drawn big in the middle of the page. Skin, muscle bellies, tendon bands and bones pop in as layers, then handwritten labels with red arrows appear on their words and the named layer turns red with striations while the camera punches in.

labels.description: 1–4 labels in narration order; each lands on its word and colours its layer red.

word.description: Narration word to land on (must appear in the narration).

focus.description: Optional final emphasis layer after the labels.

keyword.description: Narration word for the final emphasis.

note.description: Optional handwritten takeaway at the bottom (≤ 12 words).

exampleProps.title: Inside your *arm*
exampleProps.note: the tendon is the weak link until you train it

exampleNarration: Cut an arm open and you find three things. Muscle, which grows fast. Tendon, which grows slow. And bone. The tendon is the cable, and a thicker cable is what actually makes you stronger.

name: Lean vs Big
description: Rook, the lean athlete, and Brick, the hulking rival, face off in a strength test — tug-of-war, boulder lift, dead hang, push-ups, sprint, planche or a simple stare-down. Handwritten labels compare them, the lean figure's tendons glow red, and on the key word the loser stumbles with an impact panel and a red force arrow.

winner.description: Who wins on the key word (default lean).

keyword.description: Narration word where the outcome lands.

leanLabel.description: Handwritten label over the lean athlete (1–4 words).

bigLabel.description: Handwritten label over the big rival (1–4 words).

leanMuscle.description: Red highlight on the lean athlete (default tendons).

forceLabel.description: Optional word on the force arrow (tug only).

exampleNarration: Put a lean climber against a guy twice his size in a tug of war and everyone bets on the big guy. Then the rope moves, and the lean guy wins, because tendons transfer force and mass just sits there.

name: Transformation
description: Before → after body transformation: a soft, slouching version of the character on the left, a week counter ticking up, then on the key word an ink splash reveals the lean, flexing after-body with its muscles pulsing red, an impact shake and BEFORE / AFTER tags.

weeksLabel.description: Counter label (default WEEK; e.g. DAY, MONTH).

keyword.description: Narration word where the after-body is revealed.

beforeLabel.description: Tag under the before figure (default BEFORE).

afterLabel.description: Tag under the after figure (default AFTER).

afterMuscle.description: Red highlight on the after-body (default full).

note.description: Optional handwritten aside near the before figure (≤ 6 words).

exampleNarration: He started with zero equipment, just a floor and a bar. Push-ups, pull-ups, squats, every other day. By week twelve the difference was not just visible, it was measurable.

name: Science Stat
description: One big number in thumbnail lettering counting up on its word, with an ink diagram beside it: a red-lit tendon, muscle or bone cut-away, or a figure performing an exercise with the relevant part glowing. Handwritten label and optional sub-note.

label.description: Handwritten label under the number (2–8 words; *word* = red).

keyword.description: Narration word on which the number lands.

diagram.description: Diagram beside the number: anatomy layer or an exercising figure.

diagramLabel.description: Optional label with arrow on the anatomy diagram (1–4 words).

sub.description: Optional handwritten note under the label (≤ 12 words).

exampleProps.label: tendon stiffness in *12 weeks*
exampleProps.sub: heavy isometrics, 30 seconds, 3 times a week
exampleProps.title: The *tendon* number

exampleNarration: Here is the number that changed how I train. Heavy isometric holds increased tendon stiffness by up to four times in twelve weeks. Thirty seconds, three times a week, and the cable gets thicker.

name: Routine List
description: A workout routine as an ink list: each row has a tiny figure looping the exercise with its muscle in red, the exercise name in handwriting, and sets × reps in bold red. Rows slide in on their words with a red tick; in landscape a big hero figure switches to each exercise as it appears.

word.description: Narration word the row lands on.

note.description: Optional handwritten note at the bottom (≤ 10 words).

exampleNarration: The whole routine fits on a napkin. Three sets of twelve push-ups. Three sets of six pull-ups. Three sets of fifteen squats. And finish with two dead hangs of thirty seconds. Rest ninety seconds between sets.

name: Myth vs Fact
description: Split page: on the MYTH side the big rival flexes next to the handwritten myth, which gets a big red X on its word; then an ink splash reveals the FACT side where the lean athlete performs the exercise with the real muscle glowing red and a red tick.

mythWord.description: Narration word where the myth is crossed out.

factWord.description: Narration word where the fact appears.

exercise.description: Exercise shown on the fact side.

muscle.description: Red highlight on the fact side.

title.description: Optional small title at the bottom.

exampleNarration: The myth is that bigger muscles automatically make you stronger. The fact is that your tendons set the ceiling, which is why a lean climber can out-pull a bodybuilder.

name: Form Check
description: Correct form versus wrong form: two copies of the character do the same exercise side by side, the wrong one with sagging hips, rounded back or a half rep. A red X and a handwritten note with an arrow mark the mistake on its word, then a red tick and a muscle glow reward the correct version.

keyword.description: Narration word where the mistake is called out.

errorNote.description: Handwritten mistake note (1–4 words; default per exercise).

goodLabel.description: Tag under the correct figure (default CORRECT).

badLabel.description: Tag under the wrong figure (default WRONG).

exampleNarration: Most push-ups fail before the arms do. Let the hips sag and the core switches off, the shoulders take the load, and the rep stops counting. Keep one straight line from heel to head.

name: Effort Moment
description: The dramatic manga panel: the character strains at the peak of an exercise with concentration lines closing in, sweat and shaking, then on the key word an inverted impact frame, a red ink splash, a camera punch-in and giant slammed lettering. Use for the climax of a chapter.

exercise.description: Exercise held at its hardest point (omit for a standing strain pose).

pose.description: Static pose when no exercise is given.

word.description: Narration word where the impact lands.

sub.description: Optional handwritten line under the text (≤ 6 words).

annotation.description: Optional handwritten label with arrow after the impact (1–4 words).

exampleNarration: Three years of lean-forward holds for this one second. Shoulders over the hands, hips rising, every tendon loaded, and then you lock it.

name: Title Card
description: Chapter opener: an ink splash wipes in, giant thumbnail lettering slams on with a red kicker tag, and the character stands beside it (hands on hips, flexing or pointing) with red ink splatter behind them, talking the narration.

kicker.description: Optional red tag above the title (1–3 words, e.g. PART 2).

character.description: Who stands beside the title (default rook).

muscle.description: Optional red highlight on the character.

pulseWord.description: Optional narration word for a red pulse + shake.

exampleNarration: Part one. Why I quit the gym and switched to calisthenics, and what the science of lean strength actually says about it.

name: Progress Graph
description: A hand-drawn ink chart (wobbly axes, a red line drawn on point by point or hatched bars growing up) with handwritten axis labels, one annotation with a red arrow on the key point, and the character cheering at the end.

series.description: 1–3 series, 2–12 values each (first series is red).

xLabels.description: Optional x-axis labels (one per value, ≤ 8 chars).

annotation.description: Optional handwritten callout on one point of the first series.

character.description: Who cheers at the end (default rook).

muscle.description: Optional highlight on the character at the end.

exampleNarration: Muscle responds first, so for the first eight weeks it looks like muscle wins. Then it plateaus. Tendon adapts slowly, but it keeps going, and around week sixteen it catches up and never stops.
